from: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5): case, answer, clue inventory, alternatives
puzzle_type: Type 13: Detective scene with multiple interacting clues
logic_verification: test-c/verify_logic.py v2 (joint histories of all four cars, multiset track match, occupancy; roof assumption optional) -> test-c/logic-verification.json
case_summary: A small car park in front of a lodge/inn on a snowy night. Snow fell from 1 am to 3 am. At 2 am a car clipped the lamp post just inside the entrance, leaving a yellow paint scrape; that car is still in the car park. Four cars are parked in five numbered bays. The reader must date each car's last movement from its tyre tracks (softened = made while it snowed, sharp = made after the snow stopped, none = parked before the snow and never moved), match the paint, and rule out the stories that would let another yellow car be guilty.

public_facts.note: Wording may be polished for the image; the facts may not change. All three facts must be on the image.
public_facts.F1_snow_window: It snowed from 1 am until 3 am, then stopped.
public_facts.F2_incident: At 2 am the night porter heard a crunch: a car clipped the lamp post by the entrance and left a smear of its paint on it. That car is still in the car park.
public_facts.F3_track_rule: Every drive since 1 am left its own separate pair of tyre tracks, all still visible: softened by fresh snow if made while it was snowing, sharp if made after it stopped. Anything older is buried.
public_facts.question: Which bay holds the car that hit the lamp post?

answer: Bay 5 (the yellow car with snow on its roof and softened tracks).
solution_chain: The scrape is yellow, so the culprit is one of the yellow cars: bays 1, 4 and 5 (bay 2 is red).
The culprit was driving inside the car park at 2 am, inside the snowfall. Any track it made then is softened, not buried and not sharp.
Bay 1: snow on the roof and no tracks at all. It was parked before 1 am and never moved; a 2 am move would have left softened tracks.

Bay 4: sharp tracks and a clear roof. It arrived after 3 am. Could it have been here at 2 am, hit the post, left and come back? Leaving at 2 am would have left softened tracks out of the car park; there are none, and no softened tracks lead to bay 4.
Bay 5: softened tracks from the entrance and snow on the roof. It drove in while it was snowing. It is the only yellow car that can have been moving at 2 am. Answer: bay 5.
Bay 2 (red) also has softened tracks and so was moving during the snowfall, but the paint rules it out.

plausible_alternatives.why_tempting: Most 'suspicious' look: the only clear roof and the freshest tracks, and it is yellow.
plausible_alternatives.reason: Sharp tracks mean it arrived after 3 am. To have hit the post at 2 am it would have had to drive out during the snowfall, which would have left its own softened tracks (every drive leaves its own tracks); there are none.

plausible_alternatives.why_tempting: Softened tracks: it was moving during the snowfall.
plausible_alternatives.reason: It is red; the scrape is yellow.

plausible_alternatives.why_tempting: Yellow, and closest to the lamp post if the layout places it there.
plausible_alternatives.reason: No tracks: parked before the snow and never moved.

plausible_alternatives.answer: Bay 5 is innocent because its snowy roof shows it stood there all night
plausible_alternatives.reason: Roof snow only shows it stood still for part of the snowfall; its softened tracks show it arrived during the snowfall.

clue_inventory.content: 2 am crunch; the car left a smear of its own paint on the lamp post; that car is still in the car park.
Every drive since 1 am left its own separate, still-visible pair (no retracing, none hidden); softened = made while snowing; sharp = after; older = buried.
One single entrance/gateway to the car park. Every tyre track enters through it.
Five bays clearly numbered 1 to 5 (number boards, painted signs or kerb markers; must stay readable at 360 px even under snow).
Ground everywhere covered by an even layer of fresh snow, except where tracks are drawn.

A lamp post just inside the entrance, beside the entrance lane, with an obvious fresh yellow paint scrape and small dent at car-bumper height on the side facing the lane. The yellow must match the yellow cars and be clearly not red or orange. It must read unmistakably as a smear of transferred car paint (a scuffed streak along the post), not as an impact star, burst or symbol.
Bay 1: yellow car, roof covered in snow, no tracks anywhere near it; smooth snow around it.
Bay 2: red car, roof covered in snow, one pair of SOFTENED tyre tracks from the entrance into bay 2.
Bay 3: empty, smooth even snow, no tracks, no rectangle or patch of thinner snow.
Bay 4: yellow car, roof completely clear of snow (body colour visible), one pair of SHARP tyre tracks from the entrance into bay 4.
Bay 5: yellow car, roof covered in snow, one pair of SOFTENED tyre tracks from the entrance into bay 5.
No other tracks: no tracks leaving, no second pair to any bay, no tracks to or from bay 1 or 3, no footprints, no shovelled or ploughed areas, no other vehicles.

visibility_requirements: Softened vs sharp must be obvious at 360 px: e.g. softened = pale, blurred-looking, partly filled, low contrast; sharp = crisp, dark-edged, tread visible. A reader must never have to guess which kind a track is.
Tracks to different bays must not cross ambiguously or pass under another parked car; each pair visibly ends in its own bay.
Roof snow: bays 1, 2, 5 unmistakably snow-capped; bay 4 unmistakably bare.
Car colours: three identical yellows (bays 1, 4, 5) and one clear red (bay 2). The scrape uses the same yellow.
Bay numbers and all text readable at 360 px.
No footprints are drawn, so make that natural: e.g. the bays face a covered porch or walkway, or the drivers' route is otherwise plausibly out of the snow. Do not add footprints.
must_not_appear: Any generated vehicle, tyre track, footprint, number, letter or sign that could conflict with the deterministic evidence.
Any second lamp post or other damaged object that could be the 'lamp post'.
Snow falling in the image (it stopped at 3 am; falling snow would muddle sharp vs softened), unless clearly framed as an earlier moment, which is not allowed here.
Any hint of the answer: highlights, arrows, circled bay, difficulty label.
codex_freedom: Setting identity (lodge, inn, B&B, station car park...), country styling, season details beyond snow, time of morning/night as long as it is after 3 am.
Viewpoint (top-down, high-angle, front-on), medium and palette, provided every clue stays exact and readable.
Title, final public wording (facts unchanged), caption.
Which elements come from the generated image and which are drawn deterministically, subject to the deterministic flags above.

pipeline.image_generation: Exactly one OpenAI Images API request: gpt-image-2.6-flare, quality high, n=1, PNG, prompt sent verbatim. Size: 1024x1024, 1088x1088, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, or WIDTHxHEIGHT with multiples of 16, no side above 1536. No retries.
pipeline.composition: After generation Codex receives the actual image and authors the final 1080x1080 SVG (CairoSVG 2.9; no filters, <style>, masks, foreignObject or external files except source-image.png).
pipeline.qa: Claude checks the final PNG against every clue id above, at 1080 and 360 px, and re-runs the logic on what is actually visible.

changes: F3: 'its own pair' -> 'since 1 am left its own separate pair' to exclude a later drive retracing an older one (Codex issue 1).

verify_logic.py rewritten: v1 treated tracks as sets per bay and cars independently; v2 enumerates joint histories with track multisets and bay occupancy, so swap stories (e.g. bay-4 car leaving bay 5 at 2 am) are tested. Result unchanged: only bay 5 (Codex issue 3).
Direction of travel is not depicted and not needed: the argument uses only which pairs exist and their age (Codex issue 2, accepted as-is).
Difficulty: Codex assesses Medium with a harder return-trip objection; recorded, case not changed (Codex issue 4).

changes: F2 now states that the car left a smear of its paint on the post. Before, the paint meaning of the yellow mark rested on the drawing alone; the blind solver read the star-shaped mark as a cartoon impact burst, which makes bay 2 defensible (timing alone gives bays 2 and 5).
C4: the scrape must read as a paint smear, not an impact symbol.
